## Natural history notes

A small aquatic crambid moth characterized by pale whitish to tan wings with delicate brown markings and a slender, fragile body. In Florida, it is found around ponds, lakes, marshes, canals, ditches, and other freshwater wetlands where watermilfoil and other submerged or floating aquatic plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights near water, while the caterpillars feed on aquatic vegetation, cutting or tying plant material into shelters as they develop and helping connect freshwater plant communities with wetland insect food webs.
